note: tiny-gemma4 (bf16, q8_0) and tiny-gemma4/dense (dense-bf16, dense-q8_0) as llama.cpp's converter writes gemma4, with the keys of ggml-org/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF: head_count_kv an array per layer where the full layers have their own KV heads (tiny-gemma4), a number otherwise (dense); sliding_window_pattern; key_length / rope.dimension_count the full head, *_swa the sliding one; rope_freqs 1 for the rotating pairs of the full head, 1e30 for the others; no attn_v in the full layers of tiny-gemma4 (attention_k_eq_v); the norms as they are, the router scale as ffn_gate_inp.scale, per_expert_scale as ffn_down_exps.scale, layer_scalar as layer_output_scale.weight, gate_up_proj and down_proj as ffn_gate_up_exps / ffn_down_exps; 1-D tensors, norms and the router in F32, the matrices in BF16 (the bits of the folder: exact) or Q8_0 (quantize_row_q8_0_ref row by row, token_embd and the experts too). The expected values are those of the source folders. bad-* (the first nine with the embedding, the last norm and rope_freqs only): another architecture, per-layer embeddings, shared KV layers, a feed-forward width per layer, a rope scaling, a sliding rotary count of 8, a sliding_window_pattern of 3 layers, rope_freqs with a rotating pair after one that does not, an output.weight (an untied head), a missing blk.1.ffn_down_exps.scale, an extra blk.0.ffn_gate_shexp.weight, a sliding layer 2 without attn_v. rope44: tiny-gemma4 with a full head of 44 (random weights in the full layers) and 15 rotating pairs - the count, not a share, must reach the RoPE (2 * 15 / 44 * 44 is 29.999... in double). tokenizer: a gemma4 tokenizer alone (the five controls, the 256 byte tokens, a, b, ab, U+2581, U+2581a, <|turn>; merges a b, U+2581 a); bad-tokenizer, bad-tokenizer-x: one more byte token <0xZZ>, <0X41> (the decoder reads <0x only)
